mathgap.title: Signed 'has N more than'
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N more than Y", interpret it as X = Y + N (add N to Y). This captures the signed difference rather than an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement explicitly mentions a numeric difference using the phrase "has N more than".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "Roxanne has 1 more carrot than Dianna" as |Roxanne – Dianna| = 1 instead of Roxanne = Dianna + 1.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: For a transfer statement "X gives N to Y", subtract N from X's count and add N to Y's count, reflecting the net change for each person.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a person giving a specific number of items to another person.
mathgap.example: Treating "Scottie gives 12 carrots to Windell" as adding 12 to both Scottie and Windell instead of subtracting from Scottie and adding to Windell.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a variable for each person, translate every relevant statement into a linear equation (or inequality), and solve the resulting system simultaneously.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any puzzle with multiple constraints, especially when relational and transfer statements interact.
mathgap.example: Attempting to update counts step‑by‑step without forming equations, which leads to contradictions or incomplete solutions.

mathgap.title: Increase by factor interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "the number of X increases by k times", treat it as multiplying the original amount by k (X_new = X_original × k).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the wording indicates a multiplicative change rather than an additive one.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the number of carrots increases by 2 times" as adding 2 carrots instead of doubling the count.

mathgap.title: Equal split and redistribution handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among a set of recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient an equal share (original count divided by the number of recipients).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem states that someone distributes all of their items equally among others.
mathgap.example: Misreading "A splits all carrots equally among B and C" as giving each the original amount instead of half to each.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: When a statement uses the phrase "difference between X and Y" without qualifiers, treat it as the signed difference X – Y, preserving the order given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the phrase "difference between" appears in a relational equation.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between A and B" as |A – B| instead of A – B.

mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' in relational equations
mathgap.principle: In relational statements without a numeric amount, such as "the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to ...", interpret "Y has more than Z" as the signed difference Y – Z.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational clause contains "has more than" but no explicit number.
mathgap.example: Treating "the number of carrots that Alana has more than Alta" as Alana = Alta + 1 (numeric) instead of Alana – Alta = ... (signed difference).

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Incorporate all transfer statements as equations linking the giver's and receiver's counts before solving the rest of the relational constraints, ensuring the net effect of transfers is accounted for in the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the puzzle contains transfer statements alongside relational equations.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the transfer "Ina gives 12 carrots to Felton" when setting up the equations, which leads to inconsistent counts.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: When a problem includes both direct count statements (e.g., "X has N items") and transfer statements, treat the direct counts as the initial amounts before any transfers occur.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count and a transfer involving the same person appear in the same problem.
mathgap.example: Assuming "Dale has 2 carrots" is the final count after Dale receives a transfer, instead of the starting count.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: "The final answer is $\boxed{<integer>}$". Any deviation (e.g., missing LaTeX box, extra text) may cause the verifier to reject a correct answer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the puzzle and before returning the response.
mathgap.example: Writing "The final answer is 11." or "Answer: 11" which leads to rejection despite the integer being correct.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that a direct count reflects the state after all transfers, ignoring that transfers modify the initial amounts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as initial constraints before applying any transfer statements; incorporate transfers as separate equations.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may assign the whole amount to each recipient or ignore the division required by an equal split.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a person splits all items equally among recipients, set the splitter's count to zero and give each recipient an equal share of the original amount.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may add the transferred amount to the giver instead of subtracting it, reversing the intended flow.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: For "X gives N to Y", subtract N from X and add N to Y.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has more than' in relational equations as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets "X has more than Y" as |X – Y|, losing the sign and order information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "has more than" as a signed difference (X – Y) preserving the order given.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute difference
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the order and uses the absolute value, treating the phrase as an unsigned magnitude.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X – Y, preserving the order specified.
